title: What We Do
heading:
Four pillars,
one method.
description: Explore Pamodzi Community Initiative’s four areas of focus: education, health, climate resilience, and financial inclusion and enterprise.
html:
Pillar I · Education

Mobilising investment for quality education.

We help communities define education priorities, organise local resources and identify the technical or institutional support needed to move the work forward.

Projects are designed for community participation in planning and maintenance, with appropriate alignment to education authorities and district priorities.

Explore Walk for Education →
  • →Schools and classroom blocksConstruction and rehabilitation.
  • →Science and ICT laboratoriesPlus libraries and learning resources.
  • →Teachers' housing and sanitationThe facilities that keep staff in post.
  • →Digital learning and teacher capacityInstitutional strengthening and public-private partnerships.
Pillar II · Health

Resilient, people-centred health systems.

We help communities define health priorities and identify the professional, public and practical support required for safe, relevant initiatives.

Health work is designed to align with relevant authorities and qualified providers while keeping local needs and participation at the centre.

  • →Health Centre II, III and IV facilitiesHospitals and maternity wards.
  • →Theatres and diagnostic laboratoriesPlus staff accommodation.
  • →Equipment and ambulancesModern medical equipment and transport.
  • →Energy, water and digital healthRenewable systems, WASH and health-worker development.
Pillar III · Climate & green development

Locally led climate solutions.

We support communities to identify climate solutions that protect ecosystems while strengthening sustainable local opportunity.

Community participation is the point — partnerships can strengthen conservation, renewable energy and climate-smart development while aligning work to Uganda's climate and sustainable development commitments.

  • →Renewable energySolar, mini-hydro and biogas systems.
  • →Climate-smart agricultureIrrigation and water resource management.
  • →Afforestation and restorationLandscape restoration and green infrastructure.
  • →Waste management and educationEnvironmental education in communities.
Pillar IV · Financial inclusion & community enterprise

The foundation of the whole model.

We support community-owned financial practices that improve financial capability, encourage entrepreneurship and help members organise resources responsibly.

Savings groups, cooperatives and other member structures can create a disciplined foundation for enterprise and shared priorities, subject to the governance and legal requirements that apply.

  • →VSLAs, SACCOs and cooperativesStrengthening existing community structures.
  • →Youth and women's enterprisesEnterprise development and peer support.
  • →Financial literacy and investment readinessBusiness incubation and digital financial services.
  • →Responsible resource useClear governance for long-term community benefit.
Across every pillar

Six commitments that cut across the work.

01

Inclusion

Gender equality, youth empowerment and disability inclusion, for meaningful participation and equal opportunity.

02

Digital transformation

Innovation that improves service delivery, efficiency, knowledge sharing and access to opportunity.

03

Governance

Transparency and accountability systems that build institutional effectiveness and public trust.

04

Research and learning

Evidence-based solutions and continuous learning to improve programme impact.

05

Partnerships

Resource mobilisation frameworks that expand investment and collaboration.

06

Measurement

Monitoring, evaluation and impact measurement to track performance and demonstrate results.
